result.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
result.summary: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose $\textit{CARM}$ (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most $α$ at an $O(1/T)$ rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-$\textit{a}$ SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from $43.49\%$ to $9.38\%$ and the moving-average exceedance frequency from $47.29\%$ to $1.22\%$ at $α=0.10$, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CARM，在时序分布漂移下对科学超分辨率做自适应空间风险控制：用多个异质更新速率的专家在线聚合阈值，将空间不确定性分数转成可信掩膜，并证明掩膜条件风险的时均收敛率为 O(1/T)。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不确定性分数→受共形风险约束的可信区域掩膜」与延迟反馈下的阈值自适应，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选及 LOOK/STOP 可靠性门控提供可核查的方法线索，但研究对象是地球观测超分而非 VLM 推理。
